text:
ana: FYI I ran the new `mapshot` sampler on a bunch of long-session logs and the numbers look weird — eviction counters up but residency percentiles not dropping like we'd expect.
ryan: Can you paste the query you used? might be a labeling mismatch or sampling bias.
mira: +1, also what sampling window? long-context churn can skew per-hour rates.
nana: (typo) ana: sampler window was 5m, sampling rate 1/100. query I used:```promql
sum by(shard) (increase(kv_evictions_total[15m])) / sum by(shard) (increase(kv_pinned_bytes_total[15m]))
```
ryan: Hmm that division looks odd (evictions / pinned_bytes). try eviction rate per residency count:```promql
sum by(shard) (increase(kv_evictions_total[15m])) / sum by(shard) (kv_resident_fragments_count)
```
mira: Also add a 95p residency panel. I think our `kv_residency` metric is only sampled occasionally so the denominator is stale. we should surface `kv_residency_last_seen_timestamp` or a sample-age metric.
evict-bot: ALERT kv-eviction-rate HIGH shard=shard-3 value=312 (threshold=200)
nana: ana: OK thanks — I dug in and found the sampler was dropping fragments with size <64B which biases small-frag churn. that explains why evictions look high but residency stays. I pushed a quick fix to include small-frag maps.
ryan: Nice catch. Can we add a dashboard row: (1) eviction rate per-tenant, (2) residency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), (3) sample-age heatmap, (4) small-frag eviction counter?
mira: +1. For alerts: make two signals — spike in eviction rate AND concurrent drop in residency p95 within 10m. avoids noisy single-signal alerts.
nana: ana: I'll make a PR with three panels and add a `kv_small_fragment_evictions_total` counter. putting the sampler change behind a feature flag for canary.
ryan: If you can include the PromQL for sample-age:```promql
max_over_time(time() - kv_residency_last_seen_timestamp[1h])
```that will highlight stale samples.
mira: Also add a short runbook note: when eviction spikes + sample-age high -> pause compaction, increase sampler rate for 30m, re-evaluate.
nana: ana: sounds good. I'll file follow-up on the ops board with exact alert thresholds and a link to the PR. thanks! :thumbsup:
